title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as companies vie for contracts and navigate regulatory changes. Meanwhile, the push for space resilience funding continues amid a backdrop of persistent technological challenges.

themes.title: Launch Contracts Galore
themes.body: Rocket Lab's latest win with Japan’s iQPS adds to the growing list of launch contracts, underscoring a competitive landscape. SpaceX's $1.6 billion in military satellite orders further cements its dominance in this arena.

themes.title: Regulatory Shifts Ahead
themes.body: A proposed rule to exempt commercial launch licensing from environmental regulations could streamline operations for many players. This move may also spark debates on environmental accountability in the burgeoning space economy.

themes.title: Defense IPOs on the Horizon
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window appears to be cracking open, though L3Harris has opted to delay its missile business IPO until 2027. This cautious approach reflects the complexities of the current defense market despite surging demand.

themes.title: Space Resilience Funding Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion addition to space resilience funding signals a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. As geopolitical tensions rise, expect more focus on enhancing national security through space.
